messages:
harper: Hey all, happy to join! Quick onboarding snag: when I try `curl https://vault.redwood.ai/v1/secret/data/teams/sandbox` I get 403. Did I miss a step? :wave:

jules: welcome @harper! Usually a missing group mapping in SSO is the culprit. Did you confirm you9re in `redwood-engineers` and `project-sandbox` groups?

harper: yes i'm in both groups. i also have the developer badge in okta.

devex: @harper, we implemented a short self-serve flow last quarter. Steps: 1) visit https://secrets.redwood.internal/request and choose "onboard + dev access" template, 2) add a one-line justification + manager approval, 3) choose scopes (kv read, kv write, db-temp). After approval the vault role is auto-mapped. If you prefer, we can create the request for you 1: just DM us the repo/project name.

ops-bot: Created request S-49011 for harper. Waiting on manager approval. SLA 6h.

security: Note: dev KV secrets default TTL = 8h. For CI use KMS-wrapped secrets: format `ENV_VAR: kms:alias/redwood/ci`. If storing TF state use `alias/redwood/tf` and enable encryption in the backend config.

harper: thanks. a couple of followups: 1) can i get temporary DB creds instead of full DB_URL? 2) who actually rotates app secrets?

jules: 1) yes — we have a temp DB user service. Example: `rwdx db temp --role dev --ttl 4h` returns creds in JSON. 2) rotation: app owners are responsible for rotating app-level secrets every 90 days; infra keys (KMS) rotate yearly and are auto-rotated unless opt-out. Emergency rotations are handled by security with an incident ticket.

devex: also, for repos we enforce a `secrets:ci` tag to ensure KMS alias usage. If you9re working on infra code, ping @jules with the repo and we9ll attach the deploy role and TF KMS alias.

harper: perfect. i'll wait on the manager approval then try the CLI login. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:

security: DM sent with the KMS alias list and a short how-to.
